subject: Mature repeat-order outcomes should be assessed later using routine records.
unresolved_conditions: Routine records must reliably link first and subsequent orders to the same customer, with traceable sources and checks for gaps or contradictions.
Assessment must use a complete eight-week observation window and consistent first- and second-order definitions.
rationale: Later record assessment can provide information directly relevant to repeat purchasing. It instantiates the transferred documentary-continuity mechanism only if outcome linkage and record reliability are checked; merely waiting and consulting records does not establish continuity. The packet establishes dated order records but not reliable customer linkage or completed later observation. Such assessment measures ordering, without itself establishing satisfaction or an intervention effect.
